primary_claim: A Sparse Autoencoder trained on CLIP/ImageNet activations finds monosemantic features in YouTube thumbnails whose presence is statistically associated with view count (Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic 0.9875, p=0 on YouTube-8M), with the top feature's thumbnail group having a median view count over 6.5x the dataset median.

effect.metric: median view count multiplier for top SAE feature group vs dataset median; KS test

stated_future_work: clean up the code and make the trained model and data public if there is interest
further investigation to understand the link between views and Sparse Autoencoder features
limitations_stated: this relation may not be particularly strong or useful
It is unclear whether view increases of this magnitude are important to youtube creators
the much smaller sample size [for MrBeast] prevents us from having as much confidence as with youtube-8m
this dataset was compiled in 2018 so these images will not match current youtube thumbnail ecosystem
quote: The most strongly associated feature has a median view count > 6.5x the dataset median.
